repo_purpose: Offline-first bounded and evidence-preserving recovery of damaged text, archives, documents, PDF, images, audio, and video containers.

capability_families.boundary: Encoding-aware byte-preserving recovery, span maps, normalization, and structure diagnostics.
Streaming contained extraction and conservative bounded reconstruction/resynchronization under expansion and member budgets.
Streaming package validation and separately graded part/text/media recovery; active content remains inert.
Incremental native structure, conservative repair, partial extraction, and optional qpdf repair plus exact-output validation.
Candidate-based structural repair with independent decoder validation and derivative grading.
Native structure for common images; optional codec-dependent preview/write behavior for complex formats.
Streaming structural inspection and partial native repair/carve; FFmpeg/ffprobe conditionally enable validated copy-remux, stream extraction, and one-frame preview.
Detection/inspection and conditional 7-Zip extraction with explicit encryption, solid, and multivolume outcomes.
OLE inspection and conditional LibreOffice/soffice conversion to a natively validated inert PDF preview; no editable recovery.

safety_rules: Never write through an input path or weaken source identity checks.
Preserve existing outputs and publish only through the contained atomic writer.
Keep every expensive operation under the shared resource budget and cancellation contract.
Run optional tools only through the unified process runner; required isolation must fail closed.
Do not execute active content or guess/bypass passwords or encryption.
Do not advertise a goal until exact artifacts are published, validated, graded, persisted, and tested.
Keep extension, byte-zero, anywhere-signature, and structural evidence distinct.
Do not store raw source payloads in SQLite, JSONL, or reports.
Preserve user-owned and unrelated dirty worktree changes.
Do not stage, commit, push, create a PR, dispatch workflows, publish, release, deploy, or change remote settings without action-specific authorization.
sensitive_path_rules: Do not document or commit secrets, tokens, credentials, cookies, keys, .env contents, private URLs, or private user data.
Treat recovery outputs, databases, events, manifests, CSV, text reports, member names, hashes, and local paths as potentially sensitive.
Keep .agents and .specify local-only unless an explicit project decision changes this.
Do not add real user files as fixtures; use synthetic license-safe data.
